product_overview: A full-stack e-commerce backend for browsing premium sneakers, creating orders, and providing admin management (products, orders, catalog, uploads). The APIs use JWT for admin-protected routes and include operational endpoints for health and readiness (see PRD pages 1–6 for scope and endpoints).
core_goals: Provide a public storefront API for browsing, filtering, and retrieving sneaker products and related catalog data (brands, categories, banners).
Enable checkout by accepting orders and persisting order + order item records.
Provide JWT-protected admin APIs for managing products, orders, brands, categories, and banners, plus pre-signed S3 uploads for media.
Expose health and readiness endpoints and enforce security controls (CORS, CSP, rate limiting, JWT expiry).

features.name: Authentication
features.description: Admin authentication using JWT (HS256, 8-hour expiry). See FR-05 and Error Handling Matrix on pages 3–5 and page 10 of the PRD images for expected responses and error codes.
user_flows: POST /api/auth/login with valid admin {email,password} -> Receive 200 with JWT token and admin profile
POST /api/auth/login with valid credentials for non-admin user -> Receive 403 Non-admin access (as described in FR-05 on page 4)
POST /api/auth/login with invalid password -> Receive 401 Invalid credentials

features.name: Sneaker Catalog API (Products, Brands, Categories, Banners)
features.description: Public read APIs to list and retrieve sneaker products, brands, categories and homepage banners. Refer to FR-01 and FR-02 on page 2–3 for filters and slug behavior and to the images on pages 1–3 showing API surface.
user_flows: GET /api/sneakers with optional query params ?brand={brandId}&category={categoryId}&search={term} -> Receive 200 with array of Sneaker objects (filters applied at DB level)
GET /api/sneakers with malformed DB query (simulated DB error) -> Receive 500 server error (DB failure per FR-01)
GET /api/sneakers/:slug with existing slug -> Receive 200 with Sneaker detail
GET /api/sneakers/:slug with non-existent slug -> Receive 404 Not found (FR-02)
GET /api/brands -> Receive 200 with Brand[]
GET /api/categories -> Receive 200 with Category[]
GET /api/banners -> Receive 200 with Banner[]

features.name: Order Management (Checkout & Order Creation)
features.description: Create customer orders from the storefront. The POST /api/orders endpoint validates required billing/delivery/payment fields and creates Order and OrderItem records (see FR-04 on pages 3–4).
user_flows: POST /api/orders with valid body {items: [...], customerName, phone, address, billing details, deliveryMethod, paymentMethod} -> Receive 201 Created with Order object (order persisted)
POST /api/orders with missing required fields (e.g., no items or missing customerName) -> Receive 400 Validation error
POST /api/orders with invalid item quantity (quantity = 0) -> Receive 400 Validation error (client-side/cart rules on page 3 apply)

features.name: Admin Product & Catalog Management
features.description: Admin CRUD for sneaker products and catalog entities protected by JWT with isAdmin. PRD FR-07 and FR-09 (pages 5–6) specify endpoints and authorization rules. The running codebase exposes POST /api/admin/sneakers and admin routes under /api/admin/* (see code summary).
user_flows: POST /api/auth/login with valid admin credentials -> Receive 200 with JWT token
POST /api/admin/sneakers with Authorization: Bearer {JWT} and valid product body {modelName,price,brandId,...} -> Receive 200/201 with created Sneaker object
POST /api/admin/sneakers without Authorization header -> Receive 401 Missing/invalid token (see Error Handling Matrix page 10)
PUT /api/admin/products/:id with Authorization: Bearer {JWT} and update payload -> Receive 200 with updated Sneaker object
DELETE /api/admin/products/:id with Authorization: Bearer {JWT} -> Receive 200 (or 204) on successful deletion
PUT /api/admin/products/:id with invalid ID -> Receive 404 Resource not found (per FR-08/FR-07)

features.name: Admin Orders & Stats
features.description: Admin endpoints to list/filter orders and view dashboard stats. FR-06 and FR-08 (pages 4–5) define behavior and authorization requirements.
user_flows: POST /api/auth/login with valid admin credentials -> Receive 200 with JWT token
GET /api/admin/stats with Authorization: Bearer {JWT} -> Receive 200 with counts (products, orders, revenue, pendingOrders)
GET /api/admin/stats without token -> Receive 401 Missing/invalid token
GET /api/admin/orders?status={status}&page={n} with Authorization: Bearer {JWT} -> Receive 200 with filtered order list
PUT /api/orders/:id with Authorization: Bearer {JWT} and body {status: 'shipped'} -> Receive 200 with updated Order
PUT /api/orders/:id with invalid status value -> Receive 400 Invalid status (per FR-08)

features.name: File Upload (S3 Pre-signed URLs)
features.description: Generate pre-signed S3 upload credentials for admin image uploads. PRD FR-10 (page 6) describes signed upload key behavior; the codebase exposes /api/s3/presign (code summary).
user_flows: POST /api/s3/presign with Authorization: Bearer {JWT} and body {filename,contentType} -> Receive 200 with PresignedUploadInfo (URL, fields or signed headers)
POST /api/s3/presign without Authorization header -> Receive 401 Missing/invalid token
POST /api/s3/presign with valid token but AWS SDK error -> Receive 500 Server error (FR-10)

features.name: Health & Readiness
features.description: Operational endpoints for health and readiness checks. FR-11 (page 6) specifies /api/health and /ready behavior; readiness verifies DB connectivity and returns 503 on DB failure.
user_flows: GET /api/health -> Receive 200 with uptime JSON and basic health info
GET /ready when DB is reachable -> Receive 200 readiness OK
GET /ready when DB is unavailable -> Receive 503 DB unavailable (per FR-11 and page 6)

features.name: Rate Limiting
features.description: Global per-IP rate limiting (100 requests per 15 minutes) to protect the API. See FR-12 on page 7.
user_flows: Repeated GET /api/sneakers under the limit -> Receive 200 responses until limit reached
Repeated GET /api/sneakers exceeding 100 requests in 15 minutes from same IP -> Receive 429 Rate limit exceeded
